newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds slid to losses in late trade after a narrower U.S. March trade gap caused U.S. Treasuries to fall and triggered a slide in bund futures.
Earlier, guilder bonds had joined a wider rally in debt markets, after the FOMC left U.S. rates unchanged on Tuesday, and had seemed poised to end a three-day losing streak.
Dealers said trading had been fairly thin with some intracurve trades executed during the initial upmove then some outright buying emerging after prices came off again.
Yield spreads versus Germany were steady after the recent narrowing of the 10-year spread to -6 basis points from -10.
The narrower spread has been attributed to expectations that the Dutch government will announce on Friday a re-opening of sales of the 5.75 percent February 2007 bond on Friday.
Dealers said there was a small chance that a new five-year issue might be announced instead.

Some players believe the yield gap between the Netherlands and Germany might disappear altogether in the coming months as they expect the pace of Dutch inflation to pick up, lifting it well above rate in Germany where growth is more sluggish.
